relationships.subject: 1,4-dioxane
relationships.evidence_quote: 1,4-dioxane potentiates the capsaicin-sensitive transient receptor potential (TRP) channel TRPV1, thereby causing hyperalgesia in mouse model

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: However, the 1,4-dioxane-caused hyperalgesia was completely lost in Trpv1-/- mice (Fig. 1a, b), indicating that TRPV1 channel mediates the effect of 1,4-dioxane.

relationships.subject: M572
relationships.evidence_quote: A single residue mutation M572V abrogated the 1,4-dioxane-evoked currents while largely preserving the capsaicin responses.

relationships.subject: ruthenium red
relationships.evidence_quote: the single-channel currents evoked by 1,4-dioxane were fully blocked by TRPV1 blocker ruthenium red (RR, 10 μM, −60 mV, Fig. 2h) but not capsazepine

relationships.subject: protein kinase C
relationships.evidence_quote: This treatment caused a ~10-fold increase in the TRPV1 current evoked by 2% 1,4-dioxane (Fig. 4e)

key_findings: 1,4-dioxane directly activates and potentiates TRPV1, lowering its heat threshold and causing TRPV1-dependent thermal and mechanical hyperalgesia and paw edema in mice.
Effect is enhanced by acidification, PKC activation and inflammation, and requires TRPV1 residue M572 in the S4-S5 linker.
